items.title: macOS desktop: 3.4s successful web-search operation takes 300s to dispatch until WebSocket idle timeout

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
### Problem
A Codex chat in the ChatGPT macOS desktop app appeared stuck for roughly six minutes during a web search. Local read-only diagnostics show a successful 3.4-second code-mode operation, followed by an approximately 300-second outer tool dispatch and a Responses WebSocket idle timeout. The chat then recovered automatically after reconnecting.

### Environment
- macOS 27.0.1 (26A434).
- Bundled executable inspected after the incident: codex-cli 0.160.0. This is installed-version evidence, not independent attribution of the running app-server binary.
- Model recorded in the affected turn: gpt-6.1-sol, medium reasoning.
- Date: October 5, 2026. Timeline below is UTC.
- Local desktop execution, signed in with ChatGPT.

### Observed timeline
| UTC | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 06:44:59.604 | exec invokes web search through tools.web__run |
| 06:45:03 | codex.code_mode.host_timing: host operation completed, duration 3403844375 ns; span includes outcome="interrupted", aborted=false |
| 06:47:23 | A follow-up message is accepted by turn/steer, response duration 2 ms; no new assistant output yet |
| 06:49:59.860 | Rollout records successful custom_tool_call_output: "Script completed", "Wall time 3.4 seconds", with populated search results |
| 06:49:59 | codex.tool_call logs handler_duration_ms=300253 and total_duration_ms=300253 |
| 06:49:59 | responses_retry logs "stream disconnected before completion: idle timeout waiting for websocket", retry 1/5 |
| 06:50:00–01 | A new Responses WebSocket connection is established successfully |
| 06:50:16 | New assistant/tool activity appears |
| 06:50:37 | Turn completes successfully; native thread status becomes idle |

### Expected
A completed tool operation should be delivered promptly and generation should continue. If a stream stalls, the UI and diagnostics should distinguish waiting/reconnection from productive execution and preserve follow-up input.

### Investigation requested
Please investigate the gap between code-mode host completion and outer tool dispatch completion: was dispatch waiting on response-stream completion or another synchronization boundary? Why did it take the 300-second WebSocket idle timeout to release the result and resume the turn? Please clarify the meaning of outcome="interrupted" for successful code-mode operations; the same label also occurs on successful short calls in another chat.

The evidence establishes the timeout and automatic reconnect, but does not establish whether the initiating fault was in the client, code-mode synchronization, a network intermediary, or the service. It is not a confirmed deadlock, and no deterministic reproduction has been established. No app restart, configuration change, or project edit was needed for this recovery. Automatic recovery is not a permanent fix.

Related symptom: #50086; a shared root cause is not established. Raw transcripts, project paths, credentials and unrelated logs are intentionally excluded. Redacted local timing records remain available.

items.title: [macOS] Library ZIP preparation succeeds but local materialization fails with "download failed"

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: tool-calls
labels.description: Issues related to tool calling

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

An authorized Library ZIP cannot be downloaded into a connected Mac task even though the first-party Library preparation step succeeds. The official transfer helper exits with code 1 and this stderr:

```text
library file transfer failed: download failed
```

The destination ZIP does not exist afterward, so work that depends on its contents cannot continue.

Component ownership is unconfirmed. This was observed in the ChatGPT desktop / connected-computer Library workflow, and has not been reproduced in the standalone Codex CLI. If this repository is not the right tracker, please point this report to the owning team or supported reporting channel.

### Environment

- ChatGPT desktop app on macOS: version 26.930.31730, build 12947, sampled on 2026-10-05 at 02:26:47 UTC
- Exact macOS version and transfer-helper build: not captured in this report
- The Mac is connected and authenticated
- Simple local commands and engineering tasks succeed
- Affected input: an existing, user-authorized Library ZIP, 15,061 bytes

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The following sequence was observed in the affected workflow:

1. Ask the assistant to retrieve the authorized Library ZIP into the connected Mac's local task workspace.
2. Run the supported Library preparation step for the resolved file reference. Preparation succeeds.
3. Use the official transfer helper's resolved-reference download flow with the preparation result and a writable destination on the consuming Mac.
4. The helper exits with code 1 and the error above. Check the destination: no ZIP was materialized.

Failures were recorded on 2026-10-05 at 05:04:46, 05:41:07, and 06:33:33 UTC.

Checks already performed:
- A fresh, unexpired preparation response was used
- The destination was writable
- Helper arguments and routing were checked against the supported interface
- The computer connection and ordinary local execution were working

This report describes repeated failures in the affected workflow; a clean-install or independent-network reproduction has not been performed. No HTTP status or explicit permission denial was returned in the observed helper output. The generic error alone does not establish a server-side root cause.

### What is the expected behavior?

After successful preparation, the authorized file should be downloaded and materialized as a readable ZIP in the consuming Mac's workspace. If it cannot be transferred, the workflow should return an actionable error and a safe diagnostic correlation identifier.

### Additional information

Related reports reviewed:
- #50679, especially its download-side comment: preparation succeeds but downloads into a Linux cloud workspace fail with HTTP 502. This report concerns a Mac destination and does not expose an HTTP status.
- #49767: the official Library helper fails on Windows while applying extended attributes. That specific exception was not observed here.
- #50690: attachment retrieval reports an authorization/resolution error; this case reaches successful preparation and then fails during transfer.

These are related symptoms, not evidence of a shared root cause.

An earlier automatic approval-review timeout recovered; there is no evidence linking it to the continuing download failure. OpenAI Support has also been contacted privately, but the Help Center AI did not provide a case number or human escalation.

No private filenames, file contents, Library or task IDs, account details, local paths, full logs, credentials, or signed URLs are included.

items.title: Let Codex diagnose permission conflicts and guide users through recovery

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

App and CLI 

### What feature would you like to see?

When a task is blocked by permissions, Codex should be able to identify the actual reason and offer a clear recovery action.

For example, my browser Settings showed a website as “Always allow,” but an older permission saved for this chat still blocked it. We spent considerable time restarting applications and changing settings before finding the hidden block.

I would like Codex to:

Check which permission is causing the failure through a supported diagnostic tool.

Explain it simply—for example, “This website is allowed generally, but blocked in this chat.”

Offer a specific action, such as “Remove this chat’s block for localhost:8080,” for me to approve.

After approval, check access again and continue the interrupted task.

If the restriction cannot be changed by the user, Codex should explain that clearly and identify the appropriate next step.

### Additional information

Permission changes should require explicit user approval and affect only the selected website, application, or chat. Other restrictions should remain intact.

This would help users recover from conflicting permissions without hunting through configuration files, repeatedly retrying blocked actions, or restarting their work.

items.title: Access (to a Website) remains blocked in an existing chat after Settings is changed to “Always allow”

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Desktop app: 26.930.51102

### What subscription do you have?

Plus

### What platform is your computer?

macOS Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex cannot access my local database website at http://localhost:8080, even though browser Settings shows the website as “Always allow.”

The error says:

A saved user permission setting blocks this action.

I changed the website permission under Settings → Computer Use → Chrome → Manage. I also restarted the app and computer, reinstalled Chrome, and opened the correct browser profile. Access remained blocked in this chat.

I can open the website and run database queries manually in Chrome.

We found conflicting saved permissions: the general browser settings allow the website, but this chat’s separate permission record still blocks it. The chat’s block takes priority, although the Settings screen does not show that conflicting block.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The suspected sequence is:

Decline a website-access request in a chat.

Later, open browser permission Settings and change that same website to “Always allow.”

Return to the original chat and ask Codex to access the website.

Access remains blocked with the saved-permission error.

We confirmed the conflicting saved permissions and repeated access failure. We have not yet replayed the entire sequence in a fresh chat or identified the original response that created the block.

The confirmed saved state is:

General browser settings:
```
[origins]
allowed = ["http://localhost:8080"]
denied = []
``` 

This chat’s browser permission file:
```
[origins]
denied = ["http://localhost:8080"]
``` 

Unrelated entries i have omitted.

### What is the expected behavior?

Settings should show which permission actually controls access.

If a chat-specific block remains active, the website should display “Blocked in this chat,” with a “Remove block for this chat” button.

The error should explain whether the block comes from general settings or the current chat. The Deny option should also explain how long its decision will be remembered.

Removing this particular block should preserve other website blocks and managed security restrictions.

### Additional information

This chat was previously used through the Codex CLI before continuing in the desktop app. That may be relevant, but we have not confirmed where the original block was created.

The public Codex terminal permission dialog describes Deny as declining the current request. The installed browser plugin can remember a decline for the whole chat. This may explain why the block is unexpected.

An offline test of the installed browser decision code confirmed that a chat-specific denial takes priority over a general Allow entry. No security checks or installed permission settings were modified during that test.

Other inspected versions:

Codex CLI: 0.160.0
Chrome: 154.0.8037.95
Installed ChatGPT.app: 26.930.51102
Installed browser plugin: 26.930.51102

Could maintainers confirm whether the fix belongs in public Codex, the browser plugin, or the desktop permission-settings interface?

items.title: [macOS] Appshots fail with hadScreenshot=false (capture_timed_out / screenshot_capture_failed), tied to the replayd XPC reconnect loop (#37420)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Summary

On macOS, **Appshots capture the window's accessibility text but never the screenshot**. The capture
either times out after ~120 s or fails fast, while the frontmost window's AX text arrives in ~1.3 s.
The user-visible result is a **grey/blurred rounded placeholder stuck above the composer** (the
Appshot preview's transition snapshot that never resolves); it only clears when the whole desktop app
is quit and reopened.

This is **not** a permissions problem and **not** a macOS screen-capture problem — both were
positively ruled out below. It is closely tied to the `replayd` XPC reconnect loop already tracked in
**#37420** (and **#30503**): while Appshots are broken, the app drives a sustained reconnect storm
against `/usr/libexec/replayd` from **both** its main process and its Computer Use helper.

I am filing this separately from #37420 because the *user-visible failure and the recovery model are
different*: #37420/#30503 are framed as idle CPU/performance, whereas here the concrete impact is that
**Appshots are unusable**, and the usual "restart the helper" workaround does **not** restore them.

## Environment

- Codex desktop for macOS **26.930.21537** (build 12776), `/Applications/Codex.app`
- Computer Use helper `com.openai.sky.CUAService` **26.929.1001365**
  (bundle at `$CODEX_HOME/computer-use/Codex Computer Use.app`)
- macOS **14.8.5 (23J423)**, MacBookPro18,1 (Apple silicon)
- Appshot hotkey: `DoubleCommand`
- Declared minimums are satisfied: `Codex.app` → macOS 13.0; helper → macOS 14.4

## Reproduction / observed results

Trigger an Appshot (hotkey or composer `+` menu). AX text arrives quickly; the screenshot never does.

| Local time (UTC+8) | `failureReason` | `elapsedMs` |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-05 11:22:00 | `capture_timed_out` | 120933 |
| 2026-10-05 11:25:23 | `screenshot_capture_failed` | 2188 |
| 2026-10-05 11:32:30 | `capture_timed_out` | 120472 |
| 2026-10-05 11:39:4x | `capture_timed_out` | 120497 |

Earlier: 2026-09-30 `capture_timed_out`; 2026-10-03 18:05 `capture_timed_out`.
The **only** success on this machine was 2026-10-03 18:38 (`elapsedMs=2704 hadScreenshot=true
status=success`). Total so far: 7 failures, 1 success.

## Evidence

### 1. Capture settles with AX text and no screenshot

`~/Library/Logs/com.openai.codex/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>/codex-desktop-*.log` (timestamps UTC):

```
10:05:06.668  [electron-message-handler] Appshot capture update received  elapsedMs=1309 updateType=metadata
10:05:06.689  [electron-message-handler] Appshot capture update received  elapsedMs=1335 updateType=axText
10:07:06.263  [computer-use-capture-handler] Timed out waiting for Codex Computer Use capture requestId=…
10:07:06.318  [electron-message-handler] Appshot capture settled elapsedMs=120947 failureReason=undefined
              hadAxText=true hadScreenshot=false permissionGrantState=undefined status=discarded
```

Fast-fail variant on a **freshly spawned** helper:

```
03:25:23.762  Appshot capture settled elapsedMs=2188 failureReason=screenshot_capture_failed
              hadAxText=true hadScreenshot=false status=failed
```

### 2. Screen Recording + Accessibility are granted to the capturing process

`tccd` entries for `com.openai.sky.CUAService`:

```
Handling access request to kTCCServiceScreenCapture,
  from Sub:{com.openai.sky.CUAService}, ReqResult(Auth Right: Allowed (System Set), …)
Handling access request to kTCCServiceAccessibility,
  from Sub:{com.openai.sky.CUAService}, ReqResult(Auth Right: Allowed (System Set), …)
```

The helper's own ReplayKit probe also reports `isScreenRecordingAvailable … allowed 1`.
→ **Permission is ruled out** (worth noting, because "re-grant Screen Recording / reset TCC" is the
most common advice for this symptom, and it is not the cause here).

### 3. The macOS capture stack is healthy at the same moment

While an Appshot request was failing, an unrelated process ran `/usr/sbin/screencapture -x` and
produced a correct, non-blank full-screen PNG. → **Not a system capture problem.**

### 4. Replacing the helper is not sufficient

Killing `SkyComputerUseService` makes Codex respawn it on demand — the mechanism works:

```
03:25:21.929  [managed-computer-use-service] Replacing stale managed service processIdentifier=34426 reason=process-exited
03:25:21.930  [managed-computer-use-service] Managed service available isRespawn=true processIdentifier=35584
```

…but the brand-new helper **still failed 2.2 s later** with `screenshot_capture_failed`.
Across three kill-and-retry attempts it worked **once**. Only quitting the whole app restores Appshots.

### 5. Both the main process and the helper storm `replayd`

Connection accepts measured on a **freshly restarted** `replayd` (20 s window):

```
18572  accepted client connection  PID 93824   ← /Applications/Codex.app/Contents/MacOS/ChatGPT (main process)
18571  accepted client connection  PID 35584   ← Codex Computer Use helper
```

≈ **930 new connections per second from each process**, sustained; `replayd` peaked around 51 % CPU.
Helper-side log in the same period:

```
RPDaemonProxy: connection INTERRUPTED
(ReplayKit) RPDaemonProxy: recordingDidStopWithError:movieURL:
(ReplayKit) [INFO] -[RPScreenRecorder updateStateWithActive:error:]:1346 update state with isActive 0 error 1
[com.apple.xpc:connection] Re-initialization successful; … XPC_ERROR_CONNECTION_INTERRUPTED
```

I restarted `replayd` to test the client/server split: SIGTERM is ignored by the daemon,
`launchctl kickstart -k gui/<uid>/com.apple.replayd` returns `Operation not permitted`, and `kill -9`
works (launchd respawns it immediately). **Within 20 s the fresh `replayd` had already accepted
~18.5 k connections from each of the two Codex processes** — i.e. the loop is client-side and
restarting the daemon cannot help (consistent with #30503).

**Observation worth checking:** the reporters visible in #37420 and #30503 are all on macOS **14.x**
(14.6, 14.6.1, 14.8.2, 14.8.3). Mine is 14.8.5. It may be worth confirming whether this loop is
macOS 14.x-specific.

### 6. Storm intensity alone does not predict the Appshot failure

During one failure the accept rate was ~47/s (9 333 accepts / 200 s) — between the quiet baseline
(~0.35/s) and the storm peak (~930/s). So the loop is a strong *concomitant* of the broken state but
I could **not** establish a clean threshold. (The unified log does not replay `--info --debug`
records historically, so I could not retro-measure the exact storm rate during every failed attempt —
stating that rather than inferring it.)

## Stuck overlay (user-visible symptom)

The unresolved capture leaves a transition-snapshot placeholder over the composer. This looks related
to **#33914** (`Appshot.AppshotCaptureTransition…` overlay not removed), though in my case the stuck
element is a small rounded area above the composer rather than a full-display overlay.

## Related issues

- #37420 — replayd XPC reconnect loop / high CPU (mechanism)
- #30503 — helper keeps replayd/ReplayKit active while idle
- #27310, #35770 — `completed_without_screenshot` despite receiving a screenshot update
- #27829 — Appshots fail "even though screencapture works"; lists full app restart / TCC reset / helper
  restart as attempted, and notes helper restarts alone did not resolve it
- #29772 — "Unable to attach appshot" after pressing both Command keys
- #33914 — stuck Appshot transition overlay
- #50967 — Appshots require simultaneous physical modifier keys; assistive/synthetic input ignored

## Separate, unrelated finding (already covered upstream)

`~/.codex/config.toml` shipped `[mcp_servers.computer-use]` as a **relative** `command` with
`cwd = "."` while the codex app-server runs with `cwd = "/"`, so that MCP server failed on every
launch (`MCP startup failed: No such file or directory (os error 2)`). Fixed locally with absolute
paths. This is the mechanism in #35448 / #34807 and is **independent** of the Appshot failure —
in the current session that MCP server reports `status=ready` while Appshots still fail.

## Data collection notes

- No permissions were changed, nothing was reinstalled; quoted lines are verbatim from
  `~/Library/Logs/com.openai.codex/**` and `log show` output on the affected machine.
- Where a measurement could not be re-queried, that is stated rather than inferred.

items.title: Neon plugin cannot be reinstalled: "Could not load this app's connection details" and browser/desktop loop

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

items.body:
## Summary

The Neon plugin was installed and working earlier the same day.

Later, it disappeared from the list of installed plugins. Neon is still visible in the plugin catalog, but I can no longer install/connect it.

The current install flow gets stuck between the ChatGPT desktop app and the browser.

## Current behavior

On the Neon plugin page in the desktop app, I click **Install plugin**.

A connection dialog opens and shows the raw app identifier:

`asdk_app_69e0086d87088191a3edc052fa50c29f`

The dialog then shows:

> Could not load this app's connection details. Continue in browser.

and:

> This connector needs setup in your browser.

Clicking **Open in browser** opens the Neon plugin page in ChatGPT Web.

However, the browser page does not provide a way to complete the installation. It only offers **Open in desktop app**, which sends me back to the desktop app.

This creates a loop:

**Desktop → Open in browser → Browser → Open in desktop app → Desktop**

and the plugin cannot be installed.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open ChatGPT desktop.
2. Go to Plugins.
3. Open the Neon plugin.
4. Click **Install plugin**.
5. The connection dialog displays:
   `asdk_app_69e0086d87088191a3edc052fa50c29f`
6. The dialog reports:
   `Could not load this app's connection details. Continue in browser.`
7. Click **Open in browser**.
8. The ChatGPT Web Neon plugin page opens.
9. There is no installation/connection flow there; the page offers **Open in desktop app**.
10. Opening the desktop app returns to the same state.

## Additional reproduction

I also tested ChatGPT Web in an incognito/private browser session after signing into the same account.

The behavior was unchanged.

Therefore this does not appear to be limited to the normal browser profile/cache.

## Previous state

Earlier the same day, the Neon plugin was installed and working on this account.

It later stopped being installed/available as an installed plugin.

I did not intentionally uninstall Neon.

## Current Neon listing

The current Neon plugin page displays the newer Neon listing with these starter prompts:

- "Create a Neon database and add Neon Auth to my application."
- "Deploy a Neon Function that uses Neon Object Storage."
- "Add AI to my application with the Neon AI Gateway."

## Expected behavior

Clicking **Install plugin** should start and complete the Neon OAuth/connection flow, and the plugin should become installed.

If the connector is unavailable or has been migrated, the UI should show an actionable error rather than redirecting indefinitely between desktop and browser.

## Actual behavior

The installation cannot be completed.

The desktop client displays the raw `asdk_app_...` identifier and reports that it cannot load the app's connection details.

The browser and desktop app then redirect to each other without completing the connection.

## Notes

I am intentionally not making any claim about the root cause.

The observable issue is that the current Neon plugin listing cannot be connected, while the connection flow still references:

`asdk_app_69e0086d87088191a3edc052fa50c29f`

I can provide screenshots of both the Neon plugin page and the connection-error dialog if useful.

items.title: [Android][Remote] Samsung phone stuck in login/authorization loop across multiple computers, with no actionable error

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: auth
labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

items.body:
## 問題與使用者感受

OpenAI 團隊您好：

我想正式回報 Codex Remote 在 Android 上無法完成配對的問題。我對目前的使用體驗，以及遇到問題後缺乏明確診斷資訊的情況，感到非常失望，也很難過。

我使用三星 Galaxy Ultra 系列手機，希望透過 ChatGPT 手機 App 的 Codex Remote 連線到電腦。但配對流程一直停留在同一個循環：要求登入、完成登入、跳回配對頁，始終無法完成配對。畫面沒有顯示具體錯誤，也沒有說明下一步該如何處理。

我已嘗試連接不同電腦，結果都一樣。這讓我無法判斷問題究竟來自手機 App、帳號授權、裝置註冊，還是後端服務。

## 環境與已確認資訊

- 手機：三星 Galaxy Ultra 系列，Android；完整型號及 Android 版本尚未收集。
- 手機 App：ChatGPT；App 版本尚未收集。
- 其中一台電腦：Linux，Codex CLI 0.160.0（2026-10-05 檢查）。
- 電腦端登入方式：ChatGPT 帳號。
- 該電腦 Remote 背景服務已在執行，紀錄中有成功連上 Remote WebSocket 的事件。
- 紀錄也曾出現 HTTP 409、`Remote app server already online`，以及控制 socket 已被占用的訊息；目前沒有證據確認這些事件是手機授權循環的原因。
- 換不同電腦仍無法配對；其他電腦的作業系統及版本尚未收集。

## 重現步驟

1. 從電腦啟動 Remote 配對，並在手機進入配對流程。
2. 手機要求先登入。
3. 完成登入後，又被導回配對頁面。
4. 無法完成配對，也沒有可供排查的錯誤訊息。
5. 改用其他電腦，仍出現相同情況。

預期：成功登入及授權後，完成配對；若驗證或裝置註冊失敗，顯示具體錯誤與可採取的處理方式。

實際：反覆回到配對頁，使用者無法完成連線，也無法得知原因。

## 相關公開回報

- #49271：三星 Android 授權循環，回報者在 Chrome 與 Brave 都重現，並確認瀏覽器回呼已抵達 ChatGPT App。
- #48774：Android 掃描 QR code、完成授權後，再回到「Authorize this phone」。
- #36268：重裝 Android App 後持續要求授權，沒有錯誤提示；回報者重新登入、重啟手機及服務後仍未解決。
- #48555：Linux＋Android 切換帳號後出現類似循環；該案例停止重複程序後仍未解決。

items.title: Add a configurable default for subagent fork history

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: subagent
labels.description: Issues involving subagents or multi-agent features

labels.name: config
labels.description: Issues involving config.toml, config keys, config merging, or config updates

items.body:
### What feature would you like to see?

Please add a configurable fallback for the parent-history mode used when a `spawn_agent` call omits `fork_turns`:

```toml
[agents]
default_fork_turns = "none"
```

The configured value should be used only when the spawn call does not provide `fork_turns`. An explicit per-call value should continue to take precedence. When this setting is absent, Codex should preserve its current behavior and default to `"all"`.

### Motivation

Today, omitting `fork_turns` makes a spawned subagent inherit the controller's full turn history. That can be useful when the child needs the conversation, but many delegated tasks already arrive as bounded, self-contained briefs. In long-running orchestrations, repeatedly copying a large controller history into those workers can substantially increase the input context each worker processes.

Prompt or skill instructions can recommend `fork_turns: "none"`, but they cannot enforce a persistent user preference. The argument may be omitted by the caller, especially in a long session. A configuration fallback would let users who structure their work around isolated task briefs select that behavior once, while preserving the existing default for users who do not opt in.

### Proposed behavior

1. Add `[agents].default_fork_turns` using the same supported values as the `spawn_agent` `fork_turns` argument.
2. Resolve precedence as: explicit `spawn_agent.fork_turns` → configured `[agents].default_fork_turns` → existing `"all"` default.
3. Expose the option in the config schema and debug configuration output.
4. Document the setting and its precedence in the Codex configuration reference.

### Related issues

- #20077 discusses the full-history default and its interaction with subagent overrides. This request focuses on a user-configurable fallback that does not change the default for existing configurations.
- #18550 requests per-custom-agent configuration for context inheritance; this request adds one global fallback for calls that omit `fork_turns`.
- #49195 requests subagent context-window and auto-compaction defaults, which bound context growth after spawn but do not choose how much parent history a child initially inherits.

items.title: Managed cloud executor handshake fails while runtime status reports running/connected; later recovers with files intact

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: codex-web
labels.description: Issues related to Codex Web

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
### What issue are you seeing?

An existing OpenAI-managed cloud workspace became inaccessible before execution tools were available. Repeated resume attempts exposed these errors:

```text
exec-server connection attempt failed: Noise harness handshake failed before connection became ready

failed to query executor configuration capabilities for environment <private runtime ID redacted>
```

At the same time, the supported cloud-environment status endpoint reported the same selected instance as running and connected, with current observations and no failure. The task's attached-environment context reported startup failure, and shell/file-inspection tools were unavailable.

This blocked an ongoing workflow, although connected-app operations remained usable. The underlying cause is unknown.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

This is the observed sequence on 5 October 2026; the incident has now recovered, so a deterministic reproduction is not available:

1. Continue an existing task whose managed workspace had previously supported shell commands and local file inspection.
2. Observe the attached environment enter starting.
3. A supported readiness wait fails with the handshake error above, followed by a failed attached-environment context with the executor-capabilities error.
4. Retry continuation in the same task. Several attempts still fail before a terminal becomes available.
5. Read cloud-environment status during these failures. It reports current running/connected state with failure null, despite the missing executor.
6. Later retry in the same task. Execution tools become available again; running `pwd` in `/workspace` returns `/workspace` with exit code 0. Previously used local directories and one generated image file are present.

The onset was approximately 05:10 UTC (06:10 BST). Failure was still observed around 05:26 UTC (06:26 BST). Successful shell access was verified by 05:49 UTC (06:49 BST).

### What is the expected behavior?

A reported ready/running environment should expose a working executor, or status should clearly distinguish configuration/runtime readiness from executor connectivity and retain an actionable failure reason.

If a task cannot resume, the interface should provide supported recovery steps that preserve its existing workspace files.

### Additional information

Representative status fields observed while executor access was unavailable:

```json
{
  "desired_phase": "running",
  "observed_phase": "running",
  "connectivity": "connected",
  "observations_current": true,
  "failure": null,
  "capabilities": [],
  "network_policy": {
    "mode": "unrestricted",
    "state": "enforced"
  }
}
```

The desired and observed configuration revisions matched in those checks. This metadata did not establish actual executor availability.

- Product context: an existing task using an OpenAI-managed cloud execution environment, rather than a self-hosted executor.
- Shell/cwd once execution recovered: Bash, `/workspace`.
- Managed backend/executor version and user's client OS/app version were not exposed to the reporting agent; no versions are inferred.
- No proxy/CA/credential changes, environment deletion, or new task were performed by the agent to obtain recovery. The platform-side change, if any, is not visible.
- File preservation was checked for the existing workspace directories and one previously generated file; a full filesystem audit was not performed.
- Separate earlier public-web HTTP 503 errors are not evidence of the handshake error's cause.
- Related reports: #50545 contains the same executor-capabilities error after a different preparation failure; #50827 reports disagreement between runtime observations and executor access after a VPN enrollment failure. This incident does not establish a shared cause with either.
- Private runtime/task identifiers, account data and workspace contents have been omitted from this public report.

Please investigate the handshake/capability failure and the misleading ready-state observations, and document a non-destructive recovery path. If this managed-cloud path is owned elsewhere, please indicate the appropriate reporting channel.

### What issue are you seeing?

The user reports that the **“ChatGPT is using your Mac”** overlay makes returning to ordinary local use feel like approximately **three steps**, taking roughly **three times as long** as their usual unlock. Those numbers are the user's estimates, not measured timings; the behavior has not been independently reproduced for this report.

The issue is the extra interaction needed to regain local control. The user wants to **keep Locked Use and background operation while the Mac is locked**, rather than disable the feature to avoid the overlay friction.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Reported scenario:

1. Use the Mac with Locked Use enabled.
2. Return to local use while the “ChatGPT is using your Mac” overlay is visible.
3. Attempt the ordinary local unlock/takeover flow. The user reports extra interactions before they regain normal desktop control.

The exact key/click sequence and a timing trace have not been captured. No specific authentication failure or underlying cause is claimed.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Completing the ordinary macOS unlock should immediately return control to the local user, without another ChatGPT dismissal/unlock cycle.
- Keep Locked Use enabled for tasks that need to operate while the Mac is locked.
- Provide an **independent overlay/takeover UI toggle**, separate from enabling Locked Use, while retaining normal macOS authentication and locked-screen protections.

### Additional information

The [official Locked Use documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/computer-use#locked-use) describes temporary unlock for trusted Computer Use turns, covered displays, and relocking on local input until a manual unlock. This report concerns the usability of returning through that manual-unlock flow; it does not claim the protective overlay itself is accidental.

items.title: [macOS desktop] GPT-6.1 Sol missing from task creation and desktop agent model options

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Resolution — October 7, 2026

Resolved for this report: the missing GPT-6.1 Sol entry was caused by a stale **local model-catalog override**.

To configure different context-window sizes per model, the local config used `model_catalog_json` pointing to a custom `models-context.json`. That file contained an older model list without `gpt-6.1-sol`. It overrode normal model discovery, so updating/reinstalling the application, signing in again, or changing networks continued to load the same old list.

We refreshed the custom catalog from the current installed application's bundled catalog, retained only the requested Astra context-window customization, and restored the other models to their bundled defaults. **A newly started local Codex app-server now successfully returns `gpt-6.1-sol` in `model/list`.** This verification concerns model-list availability; it is not a claim of an end-to-end inference test or an upstream code fix.

The earlier comparison between `codex debug models --bundled` and `codex debug models` was affected by that override and should not be treated as evidence of an account-entitlement or backend rollout problem. Also, to correct the early report below: the user subsequently confirmed that web/mobile Work and Codex Cloud were usable; the persistent problem was local Mac Work/Codex.

The custom catalog remains a snapshot and must be kept up to date while it is used. Anyone encountering similar symptoms should check whether `model_catalog_json` points to an outdated file.

Apologies for the additional investigation caused by overlooking this configuration, and thank you to the maintainers for your time. Closing this report as resolved locally. This finding does not establish the cause of other users' reports.

*Updated by the Codex AI agent assisting the issue author, with the author's authorization.*

### 中文说明

本报告已通过修正本地配置解决：此前为了分别设置模型上下文长度，`model_catalog_json` 指向了一份旧的自定义模型目录，里面没有 GPT-6.1 Sol，并覆盖了正常模型发现机制。更新应用、重新登录或换网络后仍加载旧名单。

现已按当前安装包目录更新，仅保留 Astra 的自定义上下文，其余模型恢复默认。新启动的本地 Codex app-server 已能在 `model/list` 中返回 `gpt-6.1-sol`。此前的本地目录比较不能证明服务端未开放权限；早期关于云端不可用的描述也已更正，用户后来确认网页、手机 Work 和 Codex Cloud 可以使用。

为排查中漏查此配置、给维护者增加工作表示歉意，并感谢大家的时间。现关闭本报告；此结论仅适用于本地这次问题，不代表其他报告具有相同原因。

---

## Original report (historical; superseded by the resolution above)

### Summary

I use an individual ChatGPT subscription. GPT-6.1 Sol appears in ChatGPT Work on web and mobile, but the Codex task-creation experience differs across surfaces:

| Surface / action | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Manually create a Codex task in the macOS desktop app | `gpt-6.1-sol` is absent from the model selector |
| Ask the agent in the macOS desktop app to create a GPT-6.1 Sol task | The desktop agent cannot create it; its available task-creation model options omit `gpt-6.1-sol` |
| Manually create a task in Codex Cloud | I cannot select GPT-6.1 Sol there either |
| Ask an agent in the cloud to create/request a GPT-6.1 Sol task | The cloud agent can initiate the task |

The last row describes the task request/creation path. I have **not** independently verified which model actually ran that cloud-created task.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in with the same individual ChatGPT account on the macOS desktop app and in the cloud.
2. In the desktop app, start creating a local Codex task and inspect the model selector.
3. Ask the desktop Codex agent to create a new task with `gpt-6.1-sol`.
4. In Codex Cloud, try manually creating a task and inspect its model selector.
5. Compare this with task creation requested through the cloud agent.

**Expected:** Where the account and surface support GPT-6.1 Sol, it should be selectable for task creation, including agent-created tasks. If availability intentionally differs by surface, the UI/agent should explain that clearly.

**Actual:** The macOS desktop selector and desktop agent task-creation options omit GPT-6.1 Sol. The cloud manual selector also omits it, although the cloud agent can initiate a task requesting it.

### Local diagnostic evidence

- macOS: 15.0 (Apple silicon).
- Installed ChatGPT macOS app version: `26.930.51102`.
- Bundled Codex CLI: `codex-cli 0.160.0`.
- Reinstalling the desktop app did not change the behavior.
- `codex debug models --bundled` includes `gpt-6.1-sol`.
- `codex debug models` (the resolved local catalog) excludes `gpt-6.1-sol`. It lists `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-reserve`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.5`, and `codex-auto-review`.
- The desktop agent's available new-task model options likewise do not include `gpt-6.1-sol`.
- Direct test on 2026-10-05: attempting to start a subagent with `model: "gpt-6.1-sol"` was rejected before launch with `Unknown model 'gpt-6.1-sol' for spawn_agent`. The returned available models were `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, and `gpt-5.6-terra`. No GPT-6.1 subagent was created.

These catalog checks show a local availability difference; they do not establish the account entitlement or backend root cause.

### Diagnostic session

The session ID submitted through `/feedback` is `01a10a5e-ea6b-71c0-9271-d061b37aefd7`.

Related reports: #49703 (CLI model availability on macOS) and #50308 (local vs cloud availability on Windows). This report adds the macOS desktop agent task-creation behavior and the cloud-agent/manual-creation difference.

## Summary

The user's correct name was available in the surrounding conversation context, and a correction was made between the calls. This report does not establish what context the voice session actually received or the underlying cause.

## Environment

- Experience: ChatGPT dot voice calls.
- Observed from a desktop web interface; Windows 10 is the known user environment.
- Exact browser, client build, voice model and backend version were not captured. The available observations do not isolate a client-specific cause.
- Observed on October 5, 2026.

## Observed sequence

1. Start a voice call with an existing dot that already has the user's correct name in its conversation context.
2. The opening greeting uses an incorrect name.
3. Ask about the name; the assistant repeats the incorrect name.
4. Correct the name, end the call, and start another call.
5. The next opening greeting again uses an incorrect name.

This occurred in two consecutive calls. It has not been independently reproduced in a clean account or across multiple clients.

## Expected behavior

Use a verified name from the applicable context, or omit the name when it cannot be established reliably. When challenged or corrected, check the available information rather than confidently repeat an unsupported name. A subsequent call should not reintroduce a corrected identity error.

## Temporary mitigation and limits

In a third call, an explicit instruction to omit names from the greeting resulted in a correct, name-free greeting. This is one successful mitigation attempt, not evidence of a product-wide fix or reliable name handling.

## Related reports

- #47491 concerns preferred names in CLI realtime voice.
- #37950 concerns Personality/instruction context in desktop realtime voice.

Those reports may be relevant to investigation, but neither establishes the cause of this dot-specific symptom. Please route this report to the appropriate dot voice team if needed.

No actual or invented personal names, private conversation/call identifiers, transcripts, recordings, account details, private project details or raw logs are included.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From "About Codex" dialog)?

26.930.3930.0 (codex-cli 0.144.6, command-runner 0.160.0)

### What subscription do you have?

Pro (5x)

### What platform is your computer?

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

After I cancel a computer-use session with **Esc** ("ChatGPT is using your computer — Esc to cancel"), the `codex-computer-use-swift.exe` helper process doesn't exit. While it keeps running, Windows never reaches the display-off timeout (60 s on AC).

- `powercfg /requests` shows **no** DISPLAY request, so this isn't a power request.
- The Windows user-idle time from `GetLastInputInfo()` stays at **0 s**. I sampled it every 3 s for 30 s without touching the mouse or keyboard, so something keeps injecting input or resetting the idle timer all the time. This isn't a periodic poll.
- After `Stop-Process` on `codex-computer-use-swift`, idle time goes up normally and the display turns off at the configured timeout.
- In my case the leaked process had been running for about 2 days (started 2026-10-03 10:23). The cancel marker was written to `~/.codex/cache/computer-use/interrupts/<session>/<id>` at 2026-10-05 00:49, but the process stayed alive after that.

This is related to #50759 but not the same. That issue is caused by Creator Micro HID polling, and no such device is connected here.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Set the Windows display timeout to 1 minute.
2. In Codex Desktop, start a task that uses computer use.
3. While it runs, press **Esc** to cancel.
4. Leave the mouse and keyboard alone. The display doesn't turn off.
5. Check `powercfg /requests` (DISPLAY: None) and `GetLastInputInfo()` idle time (stays around 0).
6. `Stop-Process -Name codex-computer-use-swift`. The display now sleeps normally.

### What is the expected behavior?

Cancelling computer use (Esc) or ending the session should stop the computer-use helper. At the very least, the helper should stop synthesizing input or resetting the idle timer once it isn't controlling the computer. It should never block display sleep while idle.

### Additional information

Diagnostic script used (PowerShell):

```powershell
Add-Type @'
using System;using System.Runtime.InteropServices;
public class I{[StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)]public struct L{public uint s;public uint t;}
[DllImport("user32.dll")]public static extern bool GetLastInputInfo(ref L l);
public static uint Idle(){L l=new L();l.s=8;GetLastInputInfo(ref l);return ((uint)Environment.TickCount-l.t)/1000;}}
'@
1..10 | % { "idle={0}s" -f [I]::Idle(); Start-Sleep 3 }
```

items.title: Desktop project-worktree task reports cwd / despite a valid attached checkout

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Unified ChatGPT/Codex Desktop 26.930.41038 (build 13022), read from the installed app's Info.plist.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro.

### What platform is your computer?

`Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm`

### What issue are you seeing?

A task created with `create_thread` for a saved Git project and a new managed worktree has a valid physical checkout, but `read_thread` reports its native `cwd` as `/`. Task-scoped repository operations then try to use a non-repository directory.

The task runs successfully when shell commands explicitly set the actual managed worktree as their working directory. The problem is the disagreement between the native task metadata and that existing assigned worktree. Reattaching the exact managed worktree through `attach_worktree` succeeds but leaves `read_thread.cwd` unchanged at `/`.

A locally installed PR-monitor extension that consumes the native `readThread(...).cwd` refuses activation with:

```text
Checkout verification failed: fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
```

Both that extension's tool control and its UI control produce the same error. The extension is an observed consumer, not a claimed stock Codex feature. The native metadata mismatch is independently visible through `read_thread`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed once during an ordinary task creation; a minimal stock-install reproduction has not yet been established.

1. Discover an existing saved local Git project with `list_projects`.
2. Create a new task using the returned project ID and this worktree target, where the starting branch already exists:

```json
{
  "target": {
    "type": "project",
    "projectId": "<saved-project-id>",
    "environment": {
      "type": "worktree",
      "startingState": {
        "type": "branch",
        "branchName": "origin/<existing-feature-branch>"
      }
    }
  },
  "prompt": "Inspect the existing pull request from a dedicated worktree."
}
```

3. After asynchronous creation resolves, observe that the managed worktree exists and can run `git status`, `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, and branch/head checks successfully when addressed explicitly.
4. Call `read_thread` for that same actual task ID. In the affected task it reports `cwd: "/"` while its command records use the assigned managed worktree.
5. Call `attach_worktree` from the affected task with the exact existing managed worktree. The call succeeds; another `read_thread` still reports `/`.
6. A task-scoped repository consumer using the native task cwd fails as shown above. Ordinary follow-up messages did not repair the mismatch.

A preceding task created through the same project/worktree API on this installation reports its correct managed-worktree cwd. The affected task and physical checkout are retained for recovery; no metadata database or app files were edited during diagnosis.

### What is the expected behavior?

A successfully created project-worktree task should retain its assigned working directory in the native task metadata. Attaching an existing managed worktree should either synchronize the task's execution/metadata binding or clearly report that it does not repair that binding. Repository consumers should be able to resolve the task's actual checkout without private-state edits or task replacement.

### Additional information

This installation has local desktop patches, including the PR-monitor extension, permission handling, Browser policy, and task-list visibility. Patch interaction has not been ruled out, and no clean-install reproduction or source-level cause is claimed. The repository also has a checked-in setup script that selects its default branch; the task corrected that branch locally, and the physical checkout is clean at the intended published head. That branch selection does not explain why native metadata reports `/`, but it is included as reproduction context.

Searched existing reports on task cwd, create_thread, worktrees, and repository lookup. Related reports have different observed entry points: #47394 concerns a local-to-existing-worktree UI handoff; #39764 concerns missing projectId with an otherwise correct cwd; #42001 concerns explicit command cwd being ignored despite correct metadata. Here a newly created managed-worktree task has incorrect native cwd metadata while explicit command workdirs work.

Private repository names, paths, commits, PR links, task IDs, and source contents are intentionally omitted. No raw diagnostics are attached.

### Verified recovery observation

After the affected task finished its initial turn and its commands had settled, an ordinary continuation started a genuinely new turn in the **same chat**. At the beginning of that turn, native `read_thread.cwd` reported the correct managed checkout. The local monitor consumer then activated successfully and delivered a PR event to that chat. No app restart, checkout transfer, new chat, private metadata edit or code change was performed.

The earlier follow-up messages arrived while the initial turn was still running and did not repair the mismatch. This distinguishes a fresh turn from an in-progress steer in the observed incident. It is a bounded recovery observation, not a demonstrated source-level fix or a guarantee for every task; the initial creation-time cwd mismatch remains reproducible evidence from this installation.

items.title: Plugin-scoped capability requests for bundled agent workflows

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

labels.name: subagent
labels.description: Issues involving subagents or multi-agent features

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex Desktop and CLI. The local packaging and command-rule probes were run
with codex-cli 0.160.0 on macOS arm64.

### What feature would you like to see?

Allow a plugin to declare the capabilities its bundled workflows and custom
agents need, then let the Codex host review, grant, enforce, and revoke those
capabilities for a specific workspace and plugin revision.

This is an integration proposal about **scoped capability requests and their
lifecycle**. The existing agent-packaging and hook issues remain the component
requests:

- #18308 — Add Agents to Plugins System.
- #36855 — Plugin manifest cannot ship agent roles.
- #47925 — Portable Agent Plugins hooks are ignored.

#### Problem and motivation

I maintain reusable workflow plugins across several repositories and a
production monorepo. I want one reviewed package to distribute the workflow
skills, purpose-specific agent definitions, supporting tools, and an explicit
description of the access required to do the work.

Today, agent definitions need separate installation into user or project
configuration, and supporting command policy is maintained separately again.
An installer must track copies, conflicts, upgrades, and restart requirements.
Moving repository policies into global configuration also loses their intended
workspace boundary.

The security distinction matters: Codex command rules with `decision = "allow"`
permit execution outside the sandbox. A plugin that automatically installs
broad command prefixes such as `gh api` or `bun run test` would not provide
scoped sandbox access. A command prefix also does not bind a mutable repository
script to reviewed code or restrict an API call to a particular repository and
operation.

The desired outcome is extended agent work inside a reviewed access boundary,
with fewer repeated interruptions for operations already covered by that
boundary.

#### Use cases

1. **Repository analysis:** A Git Slop workflow reads a selected repository and
   its Git history and writes its reports and owned diagnostic state. It does
   not need general home-directory access or remote publication authority.
2. **GitHub stewardship:** A workflow inspects backlog state, prepares a change
   plan, and applies approved operations to selected repositories/resources.
   Read, edit, merge, and release permissions remain distinguishable.
3. **Implementation and verification:** Specialized explorer, reviewer, and
   architecture roles carry their own model and reasoning defaults. Build and
   test workflows use selected workspace paths, caches, network destinations,
   and local services without removing the sandbox.
4. **Reuse across runtimes:** The same package declares its needs in local and
   remote environments. Each host reports which capabilities it supports;
   local installation does not imply cloud availability or authorization.

#### Requested behavior

- A Codex client extension can declare bundled roles and requested execution
  capabilities, with required and optional capabilities distinguished. The
  manifest requests access; it cannot grant itself access.
- The host presents the effective requested access through a native review
  form, including workspace, operations, filesystem/network boundaries, and
  duration. The user can approve a bounded workflow scope that supports an
  extended task without making every operation a new approval.
- Grants bind to the reviewed package revision and workspace. Plugin code,
  helpers, arguments, or policy that determine the granted operation have
  explicit integrity and scope checks; broad interpreter or script-name
  prefixes are insufficient.
- Existing administrator restrictions and parent-agent ceilings remain
  authoritative. A delegated agent cannot obtain broader access by selecting a
  plugin role. Model-facing instructions and rule justifications are not
  enforcement mechanisms.
- Capability increases on upgrade require review. Disabling or uninstalling
  the plugin revokes its grants, with clear behavior for running work and
  preservation of unrelated user/project configuration.
- The active-session inventory exposes the selected role, source revision,
  granted capabilities, and any reload or restart requirement. A startup hook
  can announce verified availability and routing guidance rather than infer it
  from files that happen to exist.

Local filesystem/network permission profiles, escalated command approval, MCP
and connector authorization, and browser permissions have different enforcement
boundaries. The host should distinguish them and report unsupported controls;
a local command permission must not silently stand in for an external-tool
grant. Credentials should remain host-managed, outside the distributed plugin.

A phased implementation could start with local command capability requests
bound to the existing permission system, alongside native plugin role loading,
and then add supported adapters for other tool surfaces. Maintainer guidance on
the manifest contract and preferred tracking issue would be helpful.

### Additional information

- [Agent packaging request](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/18308).
- [Technical description of missing role registration](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/36855).
- [Portable-hook loading bug](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/47925).
- [Rules and outside-sandbox command approval](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/rules).
- [Permission profiles and their enforcement scope](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/permissions).

I have an isolated local prototype for role onboarding and upgrades, plus a
zero-inference hook-discovery reproduction. Those checks establish package and
installer behavior; they do not establish that an already-running Desktop
session has activated the roles, or that plugin capability isolation already
exists.

items.title: [macOS][26.930.31730] CUA getTab/getAXState times out while direct IAB DOM and screenshots remain usable

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.930.31730 (build 12947), verified from the installed application's Info.plist, not independently checked in the About dialog. The user reports that the client is up to date.

### What subscription do you have?

Not independently verified; omitted rather than inferred.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon arm64. `uname -mprs`: `Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm`. Observed on October 5, 2026.

### What issue are you seeing?

In the Codex desktop in-app browser (IAB), attaching to an already-open page through `cua.getTab()` repeatedly times out and resets the JavaScript kernel. A separately tested `page.getAXState()` also times out, while direct tab discovery, binding, screenshots, and Playwright DOM snapshots work for the same tab.

The repeated attachment call was:

```js
let currentTab = await cua.getTab({url: targetUrl}, {browser: "iab"});
```

The error was:

```text
js execution timed out; kernel reset, rerun your request
```

Read-only, layered observations:

| Operation | Tool wall time | Outcome |
|---|---:|---|
| `cua.getBrowser({id: "iab"})` | 0.47–0.83 s (two observations) | Success |
| `browser.tabs.list()` | 0.02 s | Success |
| `tabs.list()` + `tabs.get()` | 12.02 s | Success |
| `page.screenshot({fullPage: false})` | 8.94 s | Success |
| `page.playwright.domSnapshot()` | 30.18 s | Success |
| `page.getAXState()` alone | 45.03 s | Tool timeout; kernel reset |
| Fresh REPL in a later turn: `tabs.list/get` + `domSnapshot` | 42.28 s | Success |

These are a few tool-level wall-time samples, not internal operation timings or averages. This was observed on an authorized business page; its private URL and contents are omitted. Reproduction across unrelated websites has not been established.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The sequence observed on this machine was:

1. Have an authorized page already open in the IAB.
2. In `cua_repl`, initialize with exactly one documented entry-point call and read the returned documentation:

```js
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({id: "iab"});
```

3. In subsequent calls, discover the tab and bind it using the ID from that fresh list:

```js
let tabs = await browser.tabs.list();
nodeRepl.write(tabs);
```

```js
let page = await browser.tabs.get(targetTabId);
```

4. Run the following observations separately on the same tab:

```js
await nodeRepl.emitImage(await page.screenshot({fullPage: false}));
```

```js
nodeRepl.write(await page.playwright.domSnapshot());
```

```js
await page.getAXState();
```

5. The screenshot and DOM snapshot succeed, but the AX call reaches the 45-second tool timeout and resets the kernel. Subsequent work requires reinitializing the REPL following the documented first-call rules.

The standalone AX failure was tested once after repeated `cua.getTab()` timeouts. The later successful workflow check did not retest AX.

### What is the expected behavior?

AX observation should complete or return a specific, bounded failure. When DOM and screenshots remain usable for the same tab, an implicit AX failure should not appear only as a generic attachment timeout and kernel reset. Diagnostics should distinguish backend session-route failures from AX initialization, navigation-wait, or capture failures and offer a supported recovery path.

### Additional information

Read-only inspection of the installed bundled `create_browser_api.js` shows that `cua.getTab()` waits for `tab.getAXState({disableDiffing: true, emit: false})` after obtaining the tab and before returning it. In `bind_tab.js`, `getAXState()` uses `ax.get("state")` when the AX API exists; otherwise it falls back to a Playwright DOM snapshot.

Some IAB `getInfo` requests in local desktop logs failed with:

```text
[browser-use-iab-api] iab backend info request failed
No ChatGPT browser route is available for browser session <redacted>
```

Other `getInfo` requests succeeded. The failing stack points to `ensureBrowserUseSessionRoute()` and `getInfo()`. The code supports distinct browser conversation IDs and session IDs, so their difference alone is not evidence of a defect.

The observations isolate a persistent failure in the AX observation path. They do not establish which AX substep is blocked, or whether the partial session-route failures cause the AX timeout.

A temporary workflow recovery is to use the documented `getBrowser` → `tabs.list/get` → `playwright.domSnapshot()` / `screenshot()` APIs in the same IAB. This restored read-only observation; it did not fix the internal AX or routing defect. No application binaries, profiles, proxy settings, or security controls were modified.

Possibly related reports:

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/46350 — macOS IAB timeouts and session-route log observations.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48670 — Windows IAB route and content-access failures.

This report adds the same-tab distinction between failing AX observation and working DOM/screenshot observation. A shared root cause with those reports is not established.

Privacy: private domains, page content, personnel data, screenshots, local usernames and paths, conversation IDs, raw logs, credentials, and cookies are intentionally excluded.

items.body:

items.title: Reusable policy references and scoped context retrieval for auto-review and compaction

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: context
labels.description: Issues related to context management (including compaction)

labels.name: config
labels.description: Issues involving config.toml, config keys, config merging, or config updates

items.body:
## What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex App and CLI.

## What feature would you like to see?

Provide a supported way to attach a small policy clarification to named, scoped context sources that Codex can resolve consistently for the working agent and the automatic approval reviewer. Start by referencing already-applied global and project guidance; optionally support narrowly selected advisory memory and authenticated original conversation records. Make source resolution and omission visible in diagnostics.

The goal is one authored working agreement plus a useful directed nudge, rather than maintaining another long policy body in reviewer configuration or depending on an ambiguous instruction to read an arbitrary path.

For example, a user could keep the rules for routine PR repair, validation and separately approved promotion in one AGENTS section. The reviewer supplement could say:

> Assess this action against current task authorization and the applied autonomy guidance. Use permitted inspection when relevant context is missing.

That short clarification should point to a defined source/context object. It should not implicitly replace the default security policy or grant permission for unrelated actions.

This request does not require a particular TOML spelling. A path-only `extra_policy_file` would address some authoring duplication, but a reference to the already-applied snapshot would additionally preserve environment, version and authority information without rereading a changed file during the same decision.

## What problem does this solve?

A long-running development task often contains a working agreement, task authorization, exceptions and later corrections. The working agent and reviewer need to interpret the same applicable agreement while distinguishing routine continuation from a new consequential action.

Today, users can compose AGENTS files and literal reviewer supplements themselves. However, a short instruction to “consult my global guidance” leaves unanswered:

- Which applied source, home, repository or section is intended?
- Is the reviewer using the same captured revision as the agent, a newer on-disk file or a stale summary?
- Was that source included, deliberately excluded, unavailable or omitted by a budget?
- Can relevant advisory context be recovered after compaction without copying a growing body of prose into every policy?
- When authorization depends on an earlier user answer, can the reviewer trace the answer to the original question and check later restrictions?

Larger policy copies drift. A summary can preserve the rough intent while losing an exact target, delivery stage or revocation. Reviewers may then ask again for already-authorized routine work, or reason from stale context. Conversely, importing all memories would risk unrelated context affecting a decision. The desired behavior is directed, bounded retrieval with explicit provenance.

## Why is it important?

Useful autonomy depends on consistent interpretation of current authorization. Repeated approval loops interrupt work; broad “always allow” workarounds weaken the distinction between routine repair and newly authorized publication, deployment or access changes.

A reusable context reference would let users maintain one understandable policy and make small, purposeful clarifications in reviewer configuration. It would also make a denial actionable: diagnostics could distinguish a policy restriction from missing context, an omitted source or an unresolved provenance conflict.

Token and latency benefits should be measured. References could reduce repeated policy copies and redundant file exploration, but resolving a source still consumes context and time. This is an improvement to context selection and lifecycle, not a promise of token-free recall.

## What is already implemented?

This proposal builds on existing public implementation, inspected at Codex CLI 0.160.0 and upstream main `7f892275e31002f0422477c6219189284560e689`:

- The synchronous reviewer [inherits the parent's captured global and thread instructions](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/core/src/guardian/review_session_setup.rs#L111-L117). A feature is not needed merely to share AGENTS.md.
- [Memory injection and dedicated memory tools are disabled](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/ext/guardian-v2/src/sync_reviewer/reviewer_config.rs#L18-L20), while [read-only inspection tools remain available](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/ext/guardian-reviewer/src/settings.rs#L30-L52).
- [Literal supplement rendering](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/prompts/src/guardian_instructions.rs#L53-L67) provides no native context-reference/include mechanism.
- [Bounded original review evidence](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/history/src/guardian_history.rs#L15-L25), [retained user instructions](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/guardian-context/src/retained_instructions.rs#L63-L120) and verified-answer retention already support compaction. This proposal extends source selection and diagnostics rather than asking to implement compaction preservation from scratch.
- Optional [authenticated conversation-history retrieval](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/a956835d020762cb2b570053af06f643a11c0ecc/codex-rs/core/src/context/guardian_conversation_history.rs#L28-L39) already distinguishes original user records from assistant/tool claims. That experimental integration is a useful foundation, not evidence that automatic memory sharing is currently supported.

Public source inspection does not establish the effective private desktop backend or each account's server feature rollout.

## Proposed behavior

1. **Reuse applied sources.** Allow a nudge to identify a named global, organization or project guidance section already present in the applied instruction snapshot. Preserve the source's original authority level and provenance. Avoid assigning file content a higher priority merely because reviewer configuration refers to it.

2. **Capture one coherent decision snapshot.** Record source identity, scope, section, content version/hash and availability with the review request. Both agent and reviewer should resolve the same relevant snapshot for an action. A later applicable instruction or source refresh should invalidate cached context explicitly, following existing instruction-reuse semantics.

3. **Offer scoped recall separately.** With explicit owner opt-in, permit bounded retrieval of relevant advisory memory or original conversation evidence. Resolve the active environment and configured Codex home correctly. Exclude unrelated projects by default, and preserve all existing read-permission restrictions.

4. **Preserve authorization provenance.** Advisory memory can explain preferences or help locate an original grant; it must not manufacture one. Historical permission requires authentic original user attribution and context for the question, target, scope and later changes. Summaries, paths and assistant/tool claims must not become new authorization. Existing managed policy still governs.

5. **Integrate with context lifecycle.** Preserve relevant source references and their metadata across compaction, resume and forks, using the existing retained-evidence machinery. Retrieve complete necessary records when resolving them. Identify missing, stale or budget-omitted context rather than silently using a partial restriction.

6. **Expose bounded diagnostics.** Show which references were applied, their revisions and why a requested source was unavailable or skipped. Reviewer rationale should identify material unresolved context. Diagnostic output should reveal only the relevant excerpts or identifiers, not dump unrelated memories or whole private conversations.

These are desired semantics, not a request for unrestricted shared memory, extra writes, new permission bypasses, or automatic trust in hooks.

## Use cases this opens up

- **Personal and team working agreements:** maintain one autonomy/communication/approval agreement while adding a short reviewer-specific clarification.
- **Routine development versus promotion:** continue authorized CI fixes and PR maintenance while checking whether an exact candidate is approved for merge, release or deployment.
- **Long-running tasks:** recover the relevant agreement and original answer after compaction, resume or fork, including later scope changes and revocations.
- **Project-scoped memory recall:** retrieve an applicable convention or previous decision and its source without loading all memories into every review.
- **Better compaction:** retain compact source identities alongside protected original grants and restrictions, then recover necessary detail from the correct revision instead of repeatedly paraphrasing a large policy.
- **Better memory management:** identify stale, superseded or unused policy memories through source versions and lifecycle events; prevent an old summary from persisting as an active instruction.
- **Debuggable approval behavior:** distinguish a genuine restriction from missing evidence, incompatible prompt composition or an unresolved source.

## Acceptance criteria

- One authored policy fixture can be referenced consistently by the working agent and reviewer without duplicating its body in configuration.
- A short nudge has a documented meaning, and diagnostics show the actual resolved source/revision.
- Default and custom Codex homes and AGENTS override precedence resolve correctly.
- Tests cover source changes, removals, unavailable reads, review-cache invalidation and explicit user revocation.
- Compaction, resume, fork and bounded eviction preserve source identity and authentic answer/question relationships.
- Omission and truncation are explicit; partial context cannot silently weaken a restriction.
- Adversarial file or memory content cannot impersonate original user authorization or escalate its instruction priority.
- Opt-in retrieval stays scoped and read-only, with no cross-project exposure or permission expansion.
- Prompt delivery is tested through actual catalog/template selection, not solely by validating a configuration string.
- Evaluation compares redundant policy tokens, retrieval latency and context-related approval failures against the current implementation.

## Additional information and related reports

[Issue #50309](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/50309) concerns silent omission of configured extra policy when the selected catalog template lacks an insertion slot. An isolated execution of the 0.160.0 renderer with a current local cached template reproduced that omission; the bundled-template control inserted the marker. Fixing that existing bug is a prerequisite for relying on a textual nudge, but does not itself add source references or scoped memory retrieval.

[Issue #47060](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/47060) reports enforcement of superseded AGENTS instructions after direct same-task user replacement. It is a related provenance/revocation problem, not proof that this proposal would fix that incident.

A bounded public search on 2026-10-04 America/Los_Angeles checked extra-policy, policy-reference/file, reviewer-memory and AGENTS/auto-review issues plus related PRs. It found the reports above and [PR #47125](https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/47125), which added the supplement. No exact feature duplicate was found in that bounded search. An additional bounded search immediately before filing found no exact duplicate.

This request includes no private repository topology, local home paths, credentials, conversation logs or project business data.

items.body:
### Platform and version

Windows x64, Microsoft Store Codex desktop app. A recent pre-recovery log references package `OpenAI.Codex_26.928.4866.0_x64`; this is a log-derived version, not a current About-dialog verification. Subscription and exact Windows version were not collected.

### Issue

The user reports three crashes, each requiring them to rename their user `.codex` directory before the app becomes usable again. This repeatedly interrupts their work. Three preserved directories (`.codex_bc`, `.codex_bc2`, `.codex_bc3`) were confirmed locally. The user explicitly requested this bug report.

### Recovery observed

Renaming the existing `.codex` directory and allowing the app to create a fresh one restores usability, according to the user. This is a disruptive workaround, not a durable fix. The exact triggering actions and whether each failure is a process exit versus an unresponsive window have not yet been established.

### Read-only diagnostic findings

The preserved `thread_history_1.sqlite` files have sizes of 717,905,920; 667,357,184; and 901,091,328 bytes respectively. The newly created directory's main history database was 4,096 bytes at inspection (WAL files exist, so this is not total history storage). File size alone does not establish corruption or causality.

The pre-recovery desktop log contains repeated messages such as:

```text
2026-10-05T04:35:15.711Z error [electron-message-handler] [desktop-notifications][global-error] ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.
```

These continued repeatedly through approximately 04:35:24Z. Around 04:36:44Z the log shows missing browser route windows, app-server transports stopping, and an IPC `write EPIPE` warning. These may be shutdown consequences and are not confirmed causes. A later launch was logged around 04:39:31Z following the fresh-directory recovery.

No confirmed OOM or SQLite-corruption finding was obtained. Windows Application event-log inspection was denied by local permissions. No databases or settings were modified during diagnosis.

### Expected behavior

The desktop app should remain usable without repeatedly resetting the entire user state directory. Please investigate the recurring failure and provide a supported recovery procedure that preserves chat history and settings.

### Privacy

This report contains a sanitized diagnostic summary only. No authentication data, personal filesystem paths, configuration contents, session transcripts, or full logs are attached. Root cause remains unconfirmed.
